summary: Sonam Gyatso is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shinjo Kawasaki and Chogye Shabdrung. He served as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1961–1968) and held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Jamtsho is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who taught Gembo Dorji. As of 2026, he is a doctoral local researcher and Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg.

Sonam Kachru, specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He held fellowships at Forum Transregionale Studien and MPIWG, and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Sonam Thakchoe, a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas. He also held a post at the University of Tasmania around 2003.

Sonam Tsering specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completing doctoral research under Gray Tuttle alongside several other teachers. As of 2026, he serves as Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.
Sondra L. Hausner is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she serves as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Songeun Choe is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonja Arntzen is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1970–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz. She also studied under teachers Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch completed her degrees and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg between 1986 and 2005. She held posts at Heidelberg University Library, Erlangen-Nuremberg (2007), University of Vienna (2008), and University of Munich (2009–2010).

Sonya S. Lee earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu. Specializing in art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology, she taught at Swarthmore College and Stanford, and held a post at the University of Southern California (attested 2010).

Soon-il Hwang specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA under Seung-won Seo at Dongguk University, earned a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, and later held a post at Dongguk University.

Soorakkulame Pemaratana is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the National University of Singapore under Saranindranath Tagore. As of 2026, he is a Visiting Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied at Oslo, Copenhagen, and Berlin, as well as under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Uppsala University and the University of Oslo, where he became Professor of Comparative Philology and Old Norse in 1866.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Nishioka held a post as professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

Soshuku Shibatani is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Waseda and Koyasan University (PhD ~2008–2013). He taught at Sonoda Women's University and served as a researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2015, 2026).

Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor, dean (1899), and president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soyen Shaku was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure who studied at Keio University and under several masters, notably Kosen Imakita. He served as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).

Sravana Borkataky-Varma is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD ~2011–2016). She has taught at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, Harvard, CSWR, and became Instructional Professor at the University of Houston (~2022).

Sravani Kanamarlapudi works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Washington (2019) and under Richard G. Salomon, and is a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Visva-Bharati, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966). He served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1976 to 1997.
